- key_findings_brief: "Modeling cortical volume as deviations from normative neurodevelopment improves prediction of psychiatric symptoms, and a general psychopathology factor (p-factor) may help separate disorder-general from disorder-specific biomarkers."
- key_findings_detailed: "Deviations from normative models of neurodevelopment improved the out-of-sample prediction of overall psychopathology, psychosis-positive, and fear dimensions. Overall psychopathology was associated with negative deviations in several cortical regions. Case-control comparisons for depression and ADHD showed overlapping effects that were diminished when controlling for overall psychopathology."
- key_limitations: "The study used cross-sectional data, focused on T1-weighted cortical features, and the prediction models were confounded by socioeconomic status and general intelligence."
- application_notes: "The study provides a proof of principle that using normative models can improve the predictive relationship between brain and symptom data, supporting the viability of generating standardized normative models for use across different clinical sites."
